agent: N-19 PCI Stage-3 spec — DCC + LLE + GAP design
scope: Stage-3 enhancement of N-19 PCI surrogate per spec §4.4.3 — adds DCC (Dynamic Conditional Correlation) + LLE (Largest Lyapunov Exponent) + GAP (Graph-theoretic Absorption Probability) on top of Stage-2 6/6 PASS baseline

DCC.name: Dynamic Conditional Correlation
DCC.primary_ref: Engle 2002 J Bus Econ Stat 20(3):339-350 (GARCH-DCC original); Lindquist 2014 NeuroImage 101:531 (fMRI DCC adaptation)
DCC.input: 16-channel EEG α-band (8-13Hz) bandpass-filtered time series, 60s @ 250Hz = 15000 samples per channel
algorithm: 1. Per-channel univariate GARCH(1,1) fit -> standardized residuals η_i(t) = ε_i(t)/σ_i(t)
2. Compute Q(t) = (1-α-β)·Q̄ + α·η(t-1)η(t-1)' + β·Q(t-1) where Q̄ = unconditional cov(η)
3. Normalize: R(t) = diag(Q)^(-1/2) · Q(t) · diag(Q)^(-1/2)  -> 16x16 time-varying correlation matrix
4. Per-window Shannon entropy of off-diagonal R(t) values (binned 20 bins on [-1,1])
5. DCC_entropy_session = mean over t of H(R(t)_offdiag)
DCC.interpretation: High DCC entropy = rich time-varying covariance landscape (consciousness signature per Lindquist 2014); low DCC entropy = static / collapsed dynamics
DCC.normalization: DCC_entropy raw bound [0, log2(20)] = [0, 4.32]; DCC_norm = DCC_entropy / 4.32 -> [0, 1]
DCC.wake_target_band_normalized: [0.55, 0.85] (extrapolation from Lindquist 2014 fMRI DCC entropy; HEXA cohort calibration TBD)
DCC.honest_caveat: Engle DCC was designed for financial returns; neuroscience adaptation literature (Lindquist 2014, Choe 2017) is sparse — N≈12 EEG/fMRI papers as of 2026. Validation regime is THIN.

LLE.name: Largest Lyapunov Exponent
LLE.primary_ref: Wolf 1985 Physica D 16:285 (full algorithm); Rosenstein 1993 Physica D 65:117 (small-data variant — preferred for 60s EEG)
LLE.input: Per-channel EEG time series (raw broadband or α-band), 60s @ 250Hz = 15000 samples
algorithm_rosenstein: 1. Phase-space reconstruction via time-delay embedding: x(t) -> X(t) = [x(t), x(t+τ), ..., x(t+(m-1)τ)] with m=10, τ from first minimum of mutual information
2. For each reference point X(i), find nearest neighbor X(j) in phase space with |i-j| > mean period (Theiler window)
3. Track separation d_ij(k) = |X(i+k) - X(j+k)| over k forward steps
4. Compute y(k) = <ln(d_ij(k))>_i averaged over reference points
5. Linear fit slope of y(k) vs k over the 'expansion window' (typically k=1..30) -> λ₁ = LLE
6. Repeat per channel; LLE_session = mean over 16 channels of λ₁
7. Bootstrap CI: 200 resamples of nearest-neighbor pair selection
LLE.interpretation: λ₁ > 0 = chaotic attractor (consciousness signature per Pritchard 1994 EEG chaos); λ₁ ≤ 0 = converging / periodic dynamics
LLE.normalization: LLE raw bounded by sampling rate; for 250Hz EEG, expected wake λ₁ ∈ [0.05, 0.5] bits/sample (Stam 2005); LLE_norm = clip(λ₁ / 0.5, 0, 1)
LLE.honest_caveat: LLE is a single-channel chaos measure; multi-channel aggregation (mean / max / median) is non-standardized. Sleep stage 3 also shows positive λ₁ in some studies (Babloyantz 1985), so LLE alone does not separate wake from N3 — this is a Stage-3-knowable limitation.

GAP.name: Graph-theoretic Absorption Probability
GAP.primary_ref: Doyle & Snell 1984 Random Walks and Electric Networks (random walk theory); Bressler 2011 Trends Cogn Sci 15:277 (Granger causality EEG); Sporns 2018 Networks of the Brain Ch.4 (network neuroscience)
GAP.input: 16-channel EEG α-band time series (matched to DCC input)
algorithm: 1. Pairwise Granger causality F_ij computed for all 16x16 ordered pairs (model order p=8 chosen by AIC) -> directed weight matrix W
2. Threshold W at 95th percentile to retain top-edges (typically ~20 edges of 240) -> directed sparse graph G
3. Designate top-1 in-degree node as 'absorbing' state A; remaining 15 nodes are transient
4. Build transition matrix P from W (row-normalize); compute fundamental matrix N = (I - Q)^-1 where Q is the transient-to-transient block
5. Absorption probability b_i = sum_j N_ij · R_jA where R is transient-to-absorbing block; equivalently column of N·R
7. Repeat with rotating absorbing-node choice (top-3 in-degree); average GAP_variance over 3 runs
GAP.interpretation: High GAP variance = heterogeneous absorption landscape = rich directed-causal repertoire (consciousness signature per Sporns 2018 chapter on hub-richness); low GAP variance = uniform absorption = degenerate / hub-collapsed graph
GAP.normalization: GAP variance bound [0, 0.25] (var of 15 probs in [0,1] is max 0.25); GAP_norm = GAP_variance / 0.25 -> [0, 1]
GAP.wake_target_band_normalized: [0.20, 0.70] (HEXA calibration TBD — no published EEG GAP cohort exists)
GAP.honest_caveat: GAP is borrowed from random-walk / network-science (e.g. Markov chain absorption); EEG-direct application has not been published as of 2026 (literature search 0 hits 'absorption probability EEG consciousness'). This is a NOVEL Stage-3 metric — its discriminative validity is HYPOTHETICAL until cohort calibration.

stage3_formula.name: n19_pci_surrogate_v3_stage3
stage3_formula.formula: PCI_S3 = α·Stage1 + β·fluidity_norm + γ·repertoire_norm + δ·DCC_norm + ε·LLE_norm + ζ·GAP_norm
stage3_formula.weights_rationale: α=0.30 retains Stage-1 anchor (down from Stage-2's 0.50 because new metrics must collectively absorb 0.30 weight); β=0.20 (down from 0.30) keeps fluidity as second-strongest; γ=0.15 (down from 0.20); δ=0.15 elevates DCC to 4th-tier (slightly above LLE/GAP because Engle-DCC has more validation than GAP); ε=0.10 + ζ=0.10 reflect lowest-confidence novel metrics. Calibratable per session — recommended re-fit after n≥10 sessions via constrained least-squares against TMS-PCI ground truth (when available).
stage3_formula.expected_mean_rationale: Stage-2 mean was 0.555. New metric bands DCC_norm ~[0.55-0.85], LLE_norm ~[0.10-0.60], GAP_norm ~[0.20-0.70] are predicted to add net +0.0 to +0.10 versus Stage-2 (DCC pulls up, LLE/GAP slightly drag down). Predicted Stage-3 mean = 0.555 + 0.05 = 0.60 (95% CI [0.50, 0.70]).

cutoff_design.rationale: Match Stage-1 + Stage-2 cutoff for cross-stage comparability; do NOT raise cutoff to compensate for predicted higher mean — that would conflate cutoff-shift with metric-discrimination
cutoff_design.discriminative_test_proposed: Stage-3 must produce HIGHER variance across the 6-epoch cohort than Stage-2 (Stage-2 std was ~0.05 across 6 epochs); if Stage-3 std ≤ Stage-2 std, the additional metrics are not adding discrimination — they are adding noise (F-PCI-1 fires).

F_PCI_1.name: Stage-3 mean regression
F_PCI_1.interpretation_if_fired: Adding DCC + LLE + GAP REGRESSED the discriminator — more metrics ≠ more signal. Implies one or more new metrics is anti-correlated with consciousness in the wake regime.
F_PCI_1.remediation: Drop the lowest-correlating new metric and re-weight (Stage-3.5 ablation cycle)

F_PCI_2.name: DCC entropy null-equivalent
F_PCI_2.criterion: Mean DCC_entropy across 6 epochs < 95th percentile of phase-randomized surrogate DCC_entropy (200 surrogates per epoch)
F_PCI_2.interpretation_if_fired: Time-varying conditional correlation in real EEG is statistically indistinguishable from phase-randomized null — DCC contains no real time-variation signal at this sample length.
F_PCI_2.remediation: Increase epoch length (60s -> 180s) to give GARCH more sample points; or drop DCC from Stage-3 formula

F_PCI_3.name: LLE non-chaotic across cohort
F_PCI_3.criterion: All 6 epochs have mean LLE λ₁ ≤ 0 (non-positive)
F_PCI_3.interpretation_if_fired: No chaotic dynamics detected — wake EEG is being read as periodic / converging, contradicting the wake-chaos hypothesis (Pritchard 1994). Either the embedding parameters are wrong, or LLE on 60s 16ch EEG cannot detect wake chaos.
F_PCI_3.remediation: Re-tune embedding (m, τ) via false-nearest-neighbor + AMI; or drop LLE from Stage-3

F_PCI_4.name: GAP variance ≤ random graph baseline
F_PCI_4.criterion: Mean GAP_variance across 6 epochs ≤ mean GAP_variance of 200 Erdős-Rényi random directed graphs with matched edge count
F_PCI_4.interpretation_if_fired: Granger-derived directed graph has no richer absorption structure than a random graph — GAP is not measuring real causal organization.
F_PCI_4.remediation: Increase Granger threshold (95th -> 99th percentile) for sparser graph; or drop GAP

F_PCI_5.name: Stage-3 vs Stage-2 verdict disagreement
F_PCI_5.criterion: ≥1 epoch PASS in Stage-2 (vs 0.25 cutoff) but FAIL in Stage-3 (vs 0.25 cutoff), OR ≥1 epoch FAIL in Stage-2 PASS in Stage-3
F_PCI_5.interpretation_if_fired: Stage-3 metrics destabilize the Stage-2 verdict — the addition is not a refinement, it is a metric instability. Stage-3 cannot be considered a strict superset of Stage-2 evidence.
F_PCI_5.remediation: Investigate per-epoch component breakdown to identify which new metric flipped the verdict; require justified re-weighting

honest_c3_3_items: DCC GARCH = financial econometric model (Engle 2002 Nobel-cited bond/equity volatility tool). Neuroscience adaptation is recent (Lindquist 2014 fMRI; <15 EEG papers as of 2026). Statistical assumptions (conditionally Gaussian innovations, weak stationarity over 60s) are MARGINAL for EEG, which exhibits 1/f spectra and burst dynamics. DCC may produce artificially-low entropy on bursty wake EEG due to GARCH's variance-clumping bias.

LLE = single-channel chaos measure with non-standardized multi-channel aggregation. Mean / max / median across 16 channels each give different rankings on the same data (Stam 2005 reports σ-channel ≈ 0.3 × mean for healthy wake). Sleep N3 also shows positive λ₁ in some Babloyantz-tradition studies, so LLE does NOT cleanly separate wake from deep sleep — it separates 'has-attractor' from 'noise-dominated', which is a weaker discrimination than required for PCI surrogate.

GAP = NOVEL metric with ZERO published EEG application as of 2026 (literature search 'absorption probability EEG consciousness' returns 0 hits). The discriminative validity is purely HYPOTHETICAL until cohort calibration. Combined Stage-3 = metric-proliferation gym vs robust-signal track-record; over-fitting risk on N=6 cohort is HIGH. Recommendation: treat Stage-3 verdict as exploratory only, not as upgrade-of-record, until n≥10 cohort + TMS-lab-share cross-check (Stage-4) validates the formula.
